AppStatus.title: AppStatus

AppStatusChangedData.description:
An app instance changed lifecycle status.

Apply it only when ``status_revision`` is strictly greater than the ``AppSummary.status_revision`` of the row it
updates; on a tie the summary wins. The ``exception*`` fields describe the error that caused the change, and
are ``None`` when no error did.

status_revision.description: The app-status revision this change was written at; comparable with ``AppSummary.status_revision``.
status_revision.title: Status Revision

boot_id.description:
Identifies the hassette boot that sent the message; a new value means the server restarted. Ordering doesn't
need it, since ``status_revision`` keeps increasing across restarts; it lets a client reset state it keeps per
server process.
boot_id.title: Boot Id

app_status.description: The app's rollup status after this change, equal to the ``AppSummary.status`` read at ``status_revision``.

needs_restart.description:
Set when this change flagged the instance needs-restart (only a ``failed`` change can), so a client can show
it with the status.

AppStatusChangedData.title: AppStatusChangedData

AppsChangedData.description:
Payload for an app-list refresh broadcast over WebSocket.

Carries no fields and does not identify which apps changed — it is a refetch
signal, not a diff. Clients should treat receipt as "app status may be
stale, refetch" rather than inspect the payload.
AppsChangedData.title: AppsChangedData

ConnectedData.description:
Server state sent once, as the first message after a WebSocket connection opens.

``version`` is the server's hassette version; a client can compare it with its own to detect an upgrade.

app_count.description:
Number of app instances currently tracked (starting, running, or failed), not the number of configured apps.

Same meaning as ``SystemStatusResponse.app_count``.
app_count.title: App Count

ConnectedData.title: ConnectedData

ConnectivityData.description: Payload for a Home Assistant WebSocket connectivity event.
ConnectivityData.title: ConnectivityData

DeclaredEntity.description:
A Home Assistant button, switch or sensor an app instance declares through ``self.integration``.

Nested in ``AppInstance.entities`` on ``GET /api/apps``. Every platform shares one flat shape so a client
that meets a platform it doesn't know can skip that entity and keep the rest: ``unit``, ``device_class``,
``state_class`` and ``options`` are set for a sensor only.

key.description: The entity's key: lowercase letters, digits and ``_``, unique within its instance.
key.title: Key

default_entity_id.description: The entity id the app suggests, applied only when the entity is first created in Home Assistant.
default_entity_id.title: Default Entity Id

entity_category.description:
``config`` or ``diagnostic``: where Home Assistant files the entity on its device page. ``None`` for a
primary entity.
entity_category.title: Entity Category

device_class.description: A sensor's Home Assistant device class.
device_class.title: Device Class

state_class.description: A sensor's Home Assistant state class.
state_class.title: State Class

value.description:
A switch's on/off state or a sensor's value; ``None`` for a button and for a sensor that is unknown. A
timestamp sensor's value is an ISO 8601 string with offset, a date sensor's an ISO 8601 date.
value.title: Value

attributes.description: The state attributes the app last set with the value.
attributes.title: Attributes

DeclaredEntity.title: DeclaredEntity

EntityStateChangedData.description:
One app-declared entity's committed state changed.

``boot_id`` and ``entity_revision`` are the same counters ``GET /api/apps`` reports. Apply this message only
when its ``entity_revision`` is newer than the last one applied for the same ``boot_id``; revisions skip values,
and a lost message is repaired only by the next listing fetch. Declaration commits send no message: entities
appear and disappear only through the listing.

boot_id.description: Identifies the hassette boot that sent the message; a new value means the server restarted.
boot_id.title: Boot Id

entity_revision.description: The hassette-wide entity revision this change was committed at.
entity_revision.title: Entity Revision

entity.description: The entity's full description and new state, as the listing reports it.

EntityStateChangedData.title: EntityStateChangedData

ExecutionCompletedData.description:
Payload for execution_completed WebSocket messages.

``kind`` discriminates handler invocations from job executions.
``listener_id`` is set when ``kind='handler'``; ``job_id`` when ``kind='job'``.
ExecutionCompletedData.title: ExecutionCompletedData

data.description: App-tier executions persisted since the previous message, delivered together in one batch.
data.title: Data

ExecutionStatus.description: How a handler invocation or job execution ended.
ExecutionStatus.title: ExecutionStatus

LogHintWsMessage.description:
New log records exist; refetch them over HTTP.

Carries no records. Sent only to clients that subscribed to logs.
LogHintWsMessage.title: LogHintWsMessage

NeedsRestart.description:
Why an app instance needs a hassette restart: a teardown left work that may still be running.

Python can't stop a coroutine that ignores cancellation, so the only recovery is restarting hassette. Until
then the instance reports ``failed``. Nested in ``AppInstance`` and in the ``app_status_changed`` WS event.

reason.description: What the teardown left behind, such as the tasks still pending or why its evidence is incomplete.
reason.title: Reason

pending_tasks.description:
Names of the tasks still running when the teardown ended, including an initializer that hadn't stopped
(``resource:initialize:<unique name>``). Can be empty when the evidence is incomplete (the instance was
force-terminated, or its shutdown raised); ``reason`` says which.
pending_tasks.title: Pending Tasks

flagged_at.description: When the instance was flagged, in epoch seconds. The first flag stands until restart.
flagged_at.title: Flagged At

NeedsRestart.title: NeedsRestart

ServiceStatusData.description:
A framework service changed lifecycle status.

The ``exception*`` fields describe the error that caused the change, and are ``None`` when no error did.

ready.description: Whether the service had signalled readiness at the time of this status event.
ready.title: Ready

ready_phase.description: Human-readable description of the current readiness phase, or None if not available.
ready_phase.title: Ready Phase

ServiceStatusData.title: ServiceStatusData
